Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports modeling item transitions separately from textual similarity. [GaGNN (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2024.120623) combines group and individual transition graphs with sequential representations. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) predicts complementary products through a directed, weighted graph projected from historical user–item interactions. These motivate an inexpensive graph signal alongside SASRec, although results on complementary-product benchmarks do not establish gains on this task’s next-item HR@10.

Relation semantics require caution. [KGSCL (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107191) uses explicit Amazon substitution/complementarity metadata to guide sequence augmentation; those relations are unavailable here. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines SASRec-style sequence modeling with BERT representations of titles, descriptions and reviews, reporting reviews as the strongest textual contributor. Its findings therefore do not establish the benefit of titles/descriptions encoded from scratch under the present constraints.

Practical inference: build directed transition counts exclusively from training histories; smooth sparse edges and account for destination popularity. Combine this signal with SASRec through a validation-tuned weight or gate. Encode available titles/descriptions using randomly initialized token embeddings and pooling, trained jointly on next-item prediction; separate source and destination projections allow asymmetric relations. Compare graph-only, text-only and combined additions using macro validation HR@10. Treat learned edges as predictive associations: purchase order and lexical overlap alone cannot reliably identify substitutes, complements or product compatibility. Keep unsupported compatibility claims uncertain.

---

Recent work supports separate encoders for persistent preferences and recent intent, with adaptive fusion. [LSIDN (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) uses distinct encoders and denoising strategies for long- and short-term interests, directly addressing incidental historical interactions. [TLSTSRec (2024/2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) combines duration/spectrum timestamp representations with adaptive long–short fusion. [DSRec (September 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) proposes full-sequence Mamba for long-term interests and a time-modulated state-space encoder whose evolution depends on temporal gaps.

Purchase satisfaction requires more than monotonically decaying positive interest. [Temporal Positive and Negative Excitation (2023)](https://opus.lib.uts.edu.au/bitstream/10453/170069/2/SIGIR_23_TPNE.pdf) models purchases as potentially encouraging complements while temporarily suppressing substitutes; its relationship inputs include co-click/co-purchase information, limiting direct transfer here. [Learning to Forget (July 2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12714) proposes time-sensitive satiation gates, replenishment-history retrieval, and a self-supervised time-to-next-purchase objective. These are architectural proposals, not evidence of gains under this benchmark.

Practical synthesis: retain SASRec for recent transitions, add a pooled historical-interest branch, and learn a gate conditioned on observed time gaps. Treat candidate-dependent suppression/recovery as a hypothesis learned from training histories, not a known intent label. Repeat-purchase objectives need sufficient observed repeats; with unseen-item recommendation, exact-item replenishment has limited direct relevance. Compare fusion, temporal features, and suppression separately using the fixed macro validation HR@10; history alone cannot establish that a purchase fulfilled a need.

---

Recent work supports testing multi-negative objectives. [eSASRec (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.06450v1) reports strong SASRec results with sampled softmax; its best model also changes Transformer layers, so those gains cannot be attributed entirely to the loss. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) provides a useful alternative: generalized BCE corrects sampling-induced overconfidence, recommending 128–256 negatives and correction strength t=0.75. Probability calibration correction is distinct from identifying false-negative items.

Hardness needs control. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) combines uniform-sampling warm-up, global candidate recall and progressively adjusted negative difficulty. It highlights early training failures from immediate hard mining and false negatives among highest-scoring unseen items; stochastic selection among top-ranked candidates reduces that risk. [FENRec (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/33287/35442) likewise reports that larger negative pools can increase false-negative risk, particularly with synthesized hard negatives. Its future-interaction supervision would require restricting information to the permitted training split.

Practical inference for this task: compare unchanged SASRec with multi-negative sampled-softmax cross-entropy and gBCE, then separately test uniform warm-up followed by a mixture of uniform and stochastic hard negatives. Mask padding, target collisions and known training positives; this removes known conflicts but cannot identify every latent positive. Select negative count and hardness using the pinned macro validation HR@10, inspecting Electronics separately. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Candidate scores are dot products with shared item embeddings. Training uses next-item binary cross-entropy with sampled negatives. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
